headline: At depth one there is no chain to collapse, so the case reads as a clean control: identical source costs `bamboo` 0.553 ms/1k and `panda` 1.18, the difference being whether `css()` survives to run.

microbench.why: One styled component carrying base styles, nothing wrapped. `next-yak-9.7` folds it to a plain element and renders at 0.448 ms/1k, ahead of `vanilla`'s 0.502 because the emitted class is shorter than the hand-written one. `bamboo` and `panda` ship a byte-identical source file, one `css()` object literal inside a component, and land 2.1× apart: `bamboo` at 0.553 because its Vite plugin replaces the call with the resulting class string, `panda` at 1.18 because `css()` resolves the object on every render, 0.518 ms of component self-time. Depth is not the variable here; compilation is.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-9.7` 1,750 req/s, `vanilla` 1,560, `next-yak-css-9.7` 1,540. `bamboo` at 1,330 serves the same source `panda` serves at 522, and `panda-props` at 504 resolves a style prop per element. `emotion` at 435 re-hashes a thousand buttons per request.

attribution.why: `next-yak-9.7` costs 0.589 ms with a 0.246 ms library slice; `vanilla`, `bamboo` and `stylex-layers` report no library time at all and pay 0.22-0.28 ms of component self-time. `panda` spends 0.518 of its 0.980 ms in component self-time on the same JSX `bamboo` compiles away, 13.9 ms of a 26.3 ms JS window inside its own package. `emotion` splits the other way, 1.17 ms of library against 0.338 of component, since the hashing happens inside the library rather than in the case's code.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: 45.8-53.6 ms of pure JS in every extracted and atomic lane, no style and no layout in the span. `goober` (100 ms) and `styled-components` (105 ms) inject during hydration, 0.19-0.20 ms of recalculation plus a small layout pass. Spreads inside the fast cluster reach 52%, so it is a tie rather than a ranking.

inp.why: Pressing one button costs under 0.8 ms of span JS in every lane, and the whole field lands between 6.6 and 9.2 ms. At depth one with a low-cardinality class list there is nothing for any of these libraries to recompute.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: 70.6-90.6 ms across the lanes that ship a sheet, with spreads up to 39% inside the fast half. `emotion` (111 ms), `styled-components` (102) and `goober` (101) build their sheet before first paint, which is the only separation the measurement supports.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation, one layout, two paints everywhere; counts tie exactly. Recalc costs 0.128-0.189 ms and the ordering inside that range is a single sample.

payload.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` ships 2.67 kB gzipped with no styling JS at all, beside `vanilla`'s 2.70. The runtime lanes carry their compiler whatever the page contains, `emotion` 12.9 kB of JS and `styled-components` 13.4, and the atomic lanes carry their names in the markup, `bamboo` 2.91 kB of HTML inside 4.97 kB total against `panda`'s 3.16 inside 8.10.

nsweep.why: `next-yak-9.7` holds 1.84 ms at n=4,000 and `stylex-layers`, `bamboo` and `vanilla` follow at 2.06-2.10, all linear. `panda` reaches 4.91 ms and the 9.6.0 runtime 4.88, the two lanes that render something per element; `emotion` at 8.70 ms is the steepest.

crossCase: This is the depth-1 control for the Examples `compose-3` and `compose-6` shown below, which wrap the same button two and five more times. Following one lane down the ladder is the fastest way to read the case family: `next-yak-css-9.7` goes 0.522, 0.517, 0.517 ms/1k and does not move, `bamboo` 0.553, 0.805, 1.13 as it runs one `cx()` join per level, `stylex-layers` 0.530, 0.934, 1.36 through `styleq`, and `panda` 1.18, 2.24, 3.47 re-resolving each level's object.
